replacements.new:
This is the complete, comprehensive guide to every real-world location used across all five films, organised by region, with scene references, addresses, and travel tips for visiting each one.

Before you plan a Twilight road trip: a place can be the story's setting without being the place where the cameras filmed. This guide keeps those two things separate. Look for the Story Setting label when a location is important to Forks, Port Angeles, or another place in the story but was not the principal filming site.

🎬 Twilight Filming Locations by Movie

Twilight (2008)

The first film relied heavily on Oregon and nearby Washington locations. St. Helens, Portland, Carver, Silver Falls State Park, Vernonia, Ecola State Park, and other Oregon locations helped create the Pacific Northwest look, while Kalama High School in Washington stood in for Forks High School. Oregon Film's production records document Twilight shoots across multiple Oregon communities and parks.

Oregon Film Production Records →

New Moon (2009)

New Moon moved much of its production to British Columbia, using Vancouver-area locations and Vancouver Island. The production also filmed the Volterra sequence in Montepulciano, Tuscany, Italy. David Thompson Secondary School was used as Forks High School, while Pacific Rim locations on Vancouver Island represented the La Push area.

Eclipse (2010)

Eclipse continued the British Columbia production base, with locations including Belcarra Regional Park, the Vancouver area, and other BC locations used for forest, newborn, school, and action sequences. IMDb's production-location listing also records The Shire in Washington and Capilano University among the locations.

Breaking Dawn — Part 1 (2011)

Breaking Dawn — Part 1 expanded the production footprint again. The honeymoon storyline used locations in Brazil, including the Paraty area, while other production work took place in Louisiana and British Columbia. IMDb lists Casa em Paraty in Mamanguá Bay as the exterior location for the honeymoon house.

Breaking Dawn — Part 2 (2012)

The final film continued using British Columbia locations for many outdoor sequences, with additional production work in Louisiana. The finished movie combines real locations, constructed sets, and visual effects, so not every location seen on screen corresponds to a publicly visitable filming site.

🗺️ Real Filming Location vs. Story Location

Forks, WashingtonThe story's home base. Many recognizable first-film scenes were shot elsewhere, so do not assume every Forks landmark was used as a film set.
St. Helens, OregonA major first-film location that stood in for Port Angeles and supplied several recognizable street and house exteriors.
Vancouver, BCA major production hub for New Moon, Eclipse, and the Breaking Dawn films, with locations spread across Metro Vancouver and surrounding areas.
Montepulciano, ItalyThe real Tuscan town used for the Volterra sequence in New Moon.
Paraty, BrazilPart of the real-world production footprint for Breaking Dawn — Part 1's honeymoon material.
Private propertiesSome recognizable houses and residences are private. Treat map pins as viewing/navigation references and never trespass.

🌲 Oregon

Ecola State Park, Cannon Beach, Oregon — Coastal Scenes

Twilight (2008)

Ecola State Park on the Oregon coast is an important part of the first film's Pacific Northwest production footprint. Indian Beach provided coastal material associated with the story's La Push setting. The park is a real public destination, but it should not be confused with First Beach in La Push, Washington.
